papers.title_en: Automated Verification of Hamiltonian Simulation by Quantum Signal Processing
papers.authors: Min Lai, Yu-Fang Chen, Shih-Han Hung
papers.evidence: 对基于量子信号处理的哈密顿量模拟进行自动化验证，涉及块编码
papers.tldr: 针对基于量子信号处理的哈密顿量模拟缺乏全自动验证的问题，本文提出首个结构感知验证框架。它用符号化泡利和语义证明全零辅助位块与目标哈密顿量成比例并自动推断归一化因子，再提取QSP多项式并认证近似误差。实现可验证最多256个系统量子位的块编码，组合后电路宏展开约152万门。该工作表明利用算法结构可在较大规模上完成全自动验证。
papers.abstract_en: We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first fully automated verification framework for QSP-based Hamiltonian simulation. Our framework exploits the structure of the simulation algorithm: Hamiltonians are given as weighted sums of Pauli strings, embedded into larger unitaries through block encodings, and transformed into time-evolution operators by quantum signal processing (QSP). Using a symbolic Pauli-sum semantics for ancilla-indexed circuit blocks, our verifier proves that the distinguished all-zero ancilla block is proportional to the target Hamiltonian and infers the subnormalization factor automatically. It then verifies the QSP layer by extracting the implemented polynomial transformation and certifying its approximation error. This structure-aware abstraction is essential for scalability. Composing our verified block encoding and QSP wrapper yields an estimated macro-expanded size of about 1.52 million gates. The verifier certifies the block encoding once and checks the QSP layer through its abstract interface, without expanding the oracle calls. Our implementation verifies block encodings of structured Pauli-sum Hamiltonians with up to 256 system qubits and verifies QSP Hamiltonian-simulation instances by extracting their implemented polynomials and checking the resulting approximation bounds. These results show that fully automated verification can handle common Hamiltonian-simulation circuits at substantial scale when it exploits their algorithmic structure.

papers.title_en: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
papers.authors: Hari Hara Suthan Chittoor, Thirumalai Manimaran
papers.evidence: 面向非幺正算子的LCU期望值估计并转移经典负载
papers.tldr: 在NISQ设备上，LCU估计Tr(OAρA†)/Tr(AρA†)通常需ancilla、受控酉和随样本增长的电路执行，成本高昂。HERMES将A与O在Pauli基展开并经典采样项对，把目标量改写为未修改态ρ上的Pauli期望加权比值，无需量子实现A。结合Pauli去重与对易分组，测量设置数不随样本数增长；在H2/LiH虚时演化能量估计中匹配或超越单ancilla LCU基线，且更抗噪。
papers.abstract_en: Estimating the expectation value of an observable $O$ for a quantum state evolved under a general, possibly non-unitary, operator $A$ is a fundamental task in quantum simulation, chemistry, and variational algorithms. Existing linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) approaches implement $A$ on hardware, requiring ancilla qubits, controlled unitaries and, in randomized variants, fresh circuit executions for every Monte Carlo sample. These costs are prohibitive on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices. We propose HERMES (Hardware-Efficient Reusable Measurements for Estimating LCU-based expectation valueS), which moves the processing of $A$ entirely to the classical domain. Expanding $A$ and $O$ in the Pauli basis and sampling pairs of Pauli terms classically, HERMES rewrites $μ= \mathrm{Tr}(OAρA^{\dagger})/\mathrm{Tr}(AρA^{\dagger})$ as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli expectation values on the unmodified state $ρ$, with no ancillas, controlled unitaries, or quantum implementation of $A$. A two-level measurement reduction scheme (Pauli deduplication and commuting-group partitioning) bounds the number of distinct measurement settings independently of the sample count, unlike randomized LCU methods whose circuit executions grow linearly with it. On ground-state energy estimation of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{LiH}$ via imaginary-time evolution, HERMES matches or beats Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline using shallow circuits with no two-qubit gates beyond state preparation under qubit-wise commuting grouping. It is also more robust to noise and completes a noisy $\mathrm{LiH}$ simulation infeasible for the baseline, at the cost of classical overhead growing with the number of Pauli terms in $A$.
